newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strong dlr curbs German investor interest in gold.
newsitem.headline: Strong dlr curbs German investor interest in gold.

text.p: German gold traders said the bullion price remained vulnerable after its fall to 12-year lows but German investor interest was muted because of the strong dollar versus the mark.
"Asian buyers are taking advantage of the low price but physical demand here for coins and bullion is limited," said a trader at a bank dealing in sales to small investors.
"The picture may be slightly different in the professional and speculative trade."
He pegged gold in a short-term trading range of $321-327 an ounce. It was last at $324.50-324.90 compared with Thursday's low of $323.70, the lowest since early December 1985.
Private investors were having to pay around 599 marks per ounce for bullion but this compared with 575 marks just before Christmas 1996 when the gold price was around $370.
The dollar has meanwhile risen from 1.58 to 1.75 marks, erasing most of the potential gold price savings.
Annual turnover in the German bar/coin market is estimated at 50 tonnes.
Other traders saw the gold price under further pressure from more central bank sales, which they said would be the result of budgetary problems in western Europe.
"But a certain amount of central bank selling is normal to keep the market supplied," another trader said.
"Annual demand of 3,000 tonnes corresponds with just 2,500 tonnes of new mine production."
Bundesbank sales of gold reserves have been ruled out for the time being.
"The government is worried about the flight out of the mark ahead of the introduction of the euro," one said.
But the market was seen underpinned by the threat of mine closures if prices become too unattractive.
